test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 24 Aug 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the incorrect statements from among the following.

(i) Newland arranged the elements in the order of increasing atomic masses and gave the law of Octaves.

(ii) Sodium is the eighth element after lithium.

(iii) Calcium is the eighth element after Beryllium.

(iv) The law of Octaves was applicable only up to Magnesium, as after Magnesium every eighth element did not possess properties similar to that of the first.
solution:
The correct answer is**__ iii, iv.__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Statement (ii) is **correct** as Starting from lithium (Li), counting every element up to sodium (Na), sodium indeed is the eighth element (Li, Be, B, C, N, O, F, Na).
 
• Statement (iv) is also incorrect** **as Newlands' Law of Octaves was found to be inaccurate for elements beyond calcium, not magnesium. The significant deviation happens after calcium.
 
• Statement (iii) is** incorrect as Calcium (Ca) is actually the 17th elem**ent after Beryllium (Be), not the eighth. Therefore, statement (iii) is incorrect.
 
• Statement (i) is also correct as Newland did arrange the elements in the order of** increasing atomic masses **and gave the law of Octaves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **John Newlands **was an** English chemist** who arranged the elements in the order of **increasing atomic masses **and gave the** law of Octaves in 1864.**
 
• The law of Octaves states that** every eighth element **has **properties similar **to that of the** first element **when arranged in the order of increasing atomic masses.
 
• However, this law was applicable only up to** Calcium** and not beyond that as after Calcium, every eighth element **did not possess properties **similar to that of the first element.
 
• The modern periodic table is based on the** atomic number** of the elements and not their atomic masses.
 
• The elements are arranged in** increasing order of atomic number** in the modern periodic table.
